summary: API gateway timeouts and proxy buffering causing inference request timeouts and latency regressions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (CloudNote, dedicated) reported intermittent inference request timeouts and large apparent latency regressions for streaming generation calls. Impact: production traffic experienced failed streaming responses and 504/499 style timeouts for long-running generations.

Impact:
- Multiple downstream user requests failed to receive streaming tokens for 10-30s periods, causing product-visible errors and automated retry storms.
- Errors observed: 504 Gateway Timeout from load balancer, 499 Client Closed Request in API gateway logs, occasional 431 Request Header Fields Too Large.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (us-east-1) serving dedicated pool for CloudNote.
- API path affected: /v1/streams and /v1/completions (streaming and long-gen non-streaming).

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a streaming generate request with prompt that produces ~60-120s of token generation (long conversation).
2) Observe no data arriving at the client until the request either completes or times out.
3) Repeat under customer traffic and note intermittent 504s and 499s.

Expected behavior:
- Tokens should stream to client incrementally, no intermediate timeouts, subject to model latency SLA.

Observed behavior:
- Connection idle for extended periods despite upstream activity; client closes connection (499) or LB returns 504.
- In some runs, API gateway returned 431 on subsequent requests.
steps_to_reproduce: Observe absence of incremental tokens for >30s
Note status 504 or client 499 when client aborts

comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports increased streaming failures during sustained load after a deploy. Asking SRE to triage proxy and LB timeouts.

2026-03-01 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Started investigation. Initial hypothesis: LB idle timeout or proxy_buffering on API gateway causing buffering of streaming responses. Collecting gateway/nginx configs and access logs.
2026-03-01 - CloudNote (Customer): We saw the problem start around 08:50 UTC after you rolled an infra change. Impacting all long sessions.

2026-03-01 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Found api-gateway nginx had proxy_buffering enabled globally and client_header_buffer_size at default 1k; LB idle timeout was 60s. Reproduced locally by simulating streaming: upstream produced data but nginx did not flush until buffer threshold reached.

2026-03-02 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Deployed canary change: disabled proxy_buffering for /v1/streams, increased large_client_header_buffers and client_header_buffer_size, bumped LB idle timeout to 300s for dedicated pool. Monitoring canary.
2026-03-02 - CloudNote (Customer): Canary looks good, streaming resumed as expected. No 499/504 observed in canary subset.
2026-03-03 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Rolled change to all prod gateways for dedicated pools, added config validation in infra repo. Closing incident; follow-up tasks open.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Load balancer idle timeout (60s) closed long idle streaming connections during silent intervals of token generation.
Hypothesis 2: NGINX proxy_buffering was enabled, causing API gateway to buffer streaming chunks until buffer fills or upstream completes, resulting in long perceived idle periods on the client side.
Hypothesis 3: Large auth headers (customer SSO cookies) occasionally exceeded client header buffers leading to 431 responses.
Reproduction: Disabled buffering locally and observed incremental flushes matching upstream writes. Re-enabled buffering and reproduced stalled streaming behavior.
Config findings: api-gateway nginx.conf had proxy_buffering on for all upstreams; large_client_header_buffers set to default 4 1k. Load balancer (haproxy) timeout client 60s, server 60s.
Metrics: spike in 499/504 correlated with traffic increase at 08:45-09:10 UTC; p50/p95 request latency increased for streaming paths during that window.
Cross-references: See SUP-4821 for prior similar incident with gateway timeouts and streaming behavior.
resolution_notes: Applied canary: disabled proxy_buffering for streaming endpoints (/v1/streams), added proxy_cache_bypass for streaming responses.
Increased nginx large_client_header_buffers to 8 16k and client_header_buffer_size to 8k to mitigate 431 errors for auth headers.
Updated LB (haproxy) timeouts for dedicated pools: client/server idle timeouts increased from 60s to 300s for streaming-heavy customer pools.
Rolled changes to 10% canary, observed metrics for 4 hours, then rolled to 100% for dedicated pools. No regression detected.

Post-mortem action items: create runbook for streaming endpoint config, add automated smoke test that simulates long streaming sessions during deploys, include config check in PR review template (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/298).
